newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Kinnevik says '96 profit falls, dividend flat.
newsitem.headline: Kinnevik says '96 profit falls, dividend flat.

text.p: Swedish holding company Kinnevik said on Monday its 1996 profit after financial items fell to 159 million crowns ($20.5 million) from 1.01 billion in 1995.
The company said it proposed to leave its dividend unchanged at five crowns and repeated that it intended to list shares in its media subsidiary Modern Times Group (MTG).
Profits were hurt both by a drop in forestry subsidiary Korsnas's profit and a widening of MTG's loss.
Korsnas posted an operating profit after depreciation of 714 million crowns, down from 1.29 billion crowns a year earlier.
The forestry unit was stung by lower product prices and a firmer crown.
Korsnas's profit margin fell to 15 percent from 26 percent but it was still far higher than average for the forestry sector, Kinnevik said.
MTG's operating loss after depreciation widened to 536 million crowns from 126 million, as it was negatively affected by a sluggish advertising market.
"Development of the Swedish television advertising market was a disappointment in 1996," the company said.
"A positive development of real wages for consumers did not have a large impact on consumption, which means that the advertising market has developed more weakly than expected in 1996."
The value of Kinnevik's stake in telecoms group Millicom International Cellular S.A. rose to 5.07 billion crowns on March 14 from 3.59 billion crowns on December 31, 1996, the company said.
The company's net asset value amounted to 13.75 billion crowns on December 12 last year, or 230 crowns a share after full conversion of convertibles.
Sales rose to 9.74 billion crowns, from a proforma figure of 9.62 billion a year earlier. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004 ($ = 7.751 Swedish Crowns)
